15. He further submits that both the Courts failed to consider that in the instant case 12 out of 32 Charge Sheeted witnesses did not appeal as witness and thus, presumption can be taken that if they would have come to the Court the prosecution might not convict the appellant. Thus, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. He also submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that in the instant case finger prints of the accused were neither collected nor examined by expert and thus, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. He again submits that the conviction and sentence are based on surmise and conjecture and for the purpose of bringing safely in the dispensation of justice, it is necessary to consider the facts and circumstances of the case with justice mind and to acquit the innocent accused appellant. He adds that considering the facts and circumstances of the case, after the conviction and sentence awarded by the trial Court, the presumption of innocence of the accused appellant will continue until it is finally decided by the last Court of appeal and it is the duty of the prosecution to show the Court that the judgment and order were passed according to law and on the basis of the admitted and proved evidence on record. He submits that considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the entire case is concocted one with a view to fulfilling the ulterior motive of the informant. He also submits that the settled principle of law is that confessional statement must be voluntary, it must be true, it must be whole true, Investigating Officer, P.W.22 in his cross-examination stated in connection of 164 statement of the appellant that, “বায়েজিদকে ৭ দিনের পুলিশ রিমান্ডের আবেদন করা হয় একই সাথে বায়েজিদের ১৬৪ এর দোষ স্বীকারোক্তিমূলক জবানবন্দি রেকর্ডের জন্য ম্যাজিস্ট্রেটের নিকট পাঠানো হয়”it appears that the statement was not voluntary one and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. Finally, he submits that none of the independent and disinterested witnesses was examined in this case and there is no explanation from the side of the prosecution as to the non-production of the witnesses from the 

 place of occurrence and, as such, the convict-appellant is entitled to have the benefit of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, 1872, wherein it has been emphasized that failure to examine disinterested witnesses makes the prosecution case shaky, as being held in the case of The State Vs. Basiruddin, reported in 16 DLR 189 and that non-examination of relevant witness creates presumption under the said section and raises a question of doubt in the prosecution and benefit of this defence would go to the accused, in the same way, as held in the case of Nur Hossain Vs. the State reported in 31 DLR 405, thus, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is not sustainable in law and is liable to be interfered with.
